annectent.c: Annectent An*nec"tent (?), a. [L. annectere to tie or bind to. See Annex.] Connecting; annexing. Owen.

annelidan.c: Annelidan Annelid { An`ne*lid (?), An*nel"i*dan (?), } a. [F. annélide, fr. anneler to arrange in rings, OF. anel a ring, fr. L. anellus a ring, dim. of annulus a ring.] (Zool.) Of or pertaining to the Annelida. -- n. One of the Annelida.

annelida.c: Annelida ‖An*nel"i*da (?), n. pl. [NL. See Annelid.] (Zool.) A division of the Articulata, having the body formed of numerous rings or annular segments, and without jointed legs. The principal subdivisions are the Chætopoda, including the Oligochæta or earthworms and Polychæta or marine worms; and the Hirudinea or leeches. See Chætopoda.

annelidous.c: Annelidous An*nel"i*dous (?), a. (Zool.) Of the nature of an annelid.

anneloid.c: Anneloid An"ne*loid (?), n. [F. annelé ringed + -oid.] (Zool.) An animal resembling an annelid.

annex.c: Annex An*nex" (?), v. t. [imp. & p. p. Annexed (?); p. pr. & vb. n. Annexing.] [F. annexer, fr. L. annexus, p. p. of annectere to tie or bind to; ad + nectere to tie, to fasten together, akin to Skr. nah to bind.] 1. To join or attach; usually to subjoin; to affix; to append; -- followed by to. “He annexed a codicil to a will.” Johnson.
Annex An*nex", v. i. To join; to be united. Tooke.

Annex An*nex" (?), n. [F. annexe, L. annexus, neut. annexum, p. p. of annectere.] Something annexed or appended; as, an additional stipulation to a writing, a subsidiary building to a main building; a wing.

annexation.c: Annexation An`nex*a"tion (?), n. [Cf. F. annexation. See Annex, v. t.] 1. The act of annexing; process of attaching, adding, or appending; the act of connecting; union; as, the annexation of Texas to the United States, or of chattels to the freehold.

annexationist.c: Annexationist An`nex*a"tion*ist, n. One who favors annexation.

annexion.c: Annexion An*nex"ion (?), n. [L. annexio a tying to, connection: cf. F. annexion.] Annexation. [R.] Shak.

annexment.c: Annexment An*nex"ment (?), n. The act of annexing, or the thing annexed; appendage. [R.] Shak.

annihilable.c: Annihilable An*ni"hi*la*ble (?), a. Capable of being annihilated.

annihilate.c: Annihilate An*ni"hi*late (?), v. t. [imp. & p. p. Annihilated; p. pr. & vb. n. Annihilating.] [L. annihilare; ad + nihilum, nihil, nothing, ne hilum (filum) not a thread, nothing at all. Cf. File, a row.] 1. To reduce to nothing or nonexistence; to destroy the existence of; to cause to cease to be.

annihilation.c: Annihilation An*ni`hi*la"tion (?), n. [Cf. F. annihilation.] 1. The act of reducing to nothing, or nonexistence; or the act of destroying the form or combination of parts under which a thing exists, so that the name can no longer be applied to it; as, the annihilation of a corporation.

annihilationist.c: Annihilationist An*ni`hi*la"tion*ist, n. (Theol.) One who believes that eternal punishment consists in annihilation or extinction of being; a destructionist.

annihilative.c: Annihilative An*ni"hi*la*tive (?), a. Serving to annihilate; destructive.

annihilator.c: Annihilator An*ni"hi*la`tor (?), n. One who, or that which, annihilates; as, a fire annihilator.

anniversary.c: Anniversary An`ni*ver"sa*ry (?), a. [L. anniversarius; annus year + vertere, versum, to turn: cf. F. anniversaire.] Returning with the year, at a stated time; annual; yearly; as, an anniversary feast.

Anniversary An`ni*ver"sa*ry, n.; pl. Anniversaries (?). [Cf. F. anniversaire.] 1. The annual return of the day on which any notable event took place, or is wont to be celebrated; as, the anniversary of the Declaration of Independence.

anniverse.c: Anniverse An"ni*verse (?), n. [L. anni versus the turning of a year.] Anniversary. [Obs.] Dryden.

annodated.c: Annodated An"no*da`ted (?), a. [L. ad to + nodus a knot.] (Her.) Curved somewhat in the form of the letter S. Cussans.

anno.c: Anno Domini ‖An"no Dom"i*ni (?). [L., in the year of [our] Lord [Jesus Christ]; usually abbrev. a. d.] In the year of the Christian era; as, a. d. 1887.

annomination.c: Annomination An*nom`i*na"tion (?), n. [L. annominatio. See Agnomination.] 1. Paronomasia; punning.

annotate.c: Annotate An"no*tate (?), v. t. [imp. & p. p. Annotated; p. pr. & vb. n. Annotating.] [L. annotatus; p. p. of annotare to annotate; ad + notare to mark, nota mark. See Note, n.] To explain or criticize by notes; as, to annotate the works of Bacon.
Annotate An"no*tate, v. i. To make notes or comments; -- with on or upon.

annotation.c: Annotation An`no*ta"tion (?), n. [L. annotatio: cf. F. annotation.] A note, added by way of comment, or explanation; -- usually in the plural; as, annotations on ancient authors, or on a word or a passage.

annotative.c: Annotative An"no*ta*tive (?), a. Characterized by annotations; of the nature of annotation.

annotator.c: Annotator An"no*ta`tor (?), n. [L.] A writer of annotations; a commentator.

annotatory.c: Annotatory An*no"ta*to*ry (?), a. Pertaining to an annotator; containing annotations. [R.]

annotine.c: Annotine An"no*tine (?), n. [L. annotinus a year old.] (Zool.) A bird one year old, or that has once molted.

annotinous.c: Annotinous An*not"i*nous (?), a. [L. annotinus, fr. annus year.] (Bot.) A year old; in Yearly growths.

arnotto.c: Arnotto Annotto An*not"to (ăn*nŏt"to), Ar*not"to (är*nŏt"to), n. [Perh. the native name.] A red or yellowish-red dyeing material, prepared from the pulp surrounding the seeds of a tree (Bixa orellana) belonging to the tropical regions of America. It is used for coloring cheese, butter, etc. [Written also Anatto, Anatta, Annatto, Annotta, etc.]

announce.c: Announce An*nounce" (?), v. t. [imp. & p. p. Announced (?); p. pr. & vb. n. Announcing (?).] [OF. anoncier, F. annoncer, fr. L. annuntiare; ad + nuntiare to report, relate, nuntius messenger, bearer of news. See Nuncio, and cf. Annunciate.]

announcement.c: Announcement An*nounce"ment (?), n. The act of announcing, or giving notice; that which announces; proclamation; publication.

annoy.c: Annoy An*noy" (ăn*noi"), v. t. [imp. & p. p. Annoyed (ăn*noid"); p. pr. & vb. n. Annoying.] [OE. anoien, anuien, OF. anoier, anuier, F. ennuyer, fr. OF. anoi, anui, enui, annoyance, vexation, F. ennui. See Annoy, n.] To disturb or irritate, especially by continued or repeated acts; to tease; to ruffle in mind; to vex; as, I was annoyed by his remarks.

Annoy An*noy" (?), n. [OE. anoi, anui, OF. anoi, anui, enui, fr. L. in odio hatred (esse alicui in odio, Cic.). See Ennui, Odium, Noisome, Noy.] A feeling of discomfort or vexation caused by what one dislikes; also, whatever causes such a feeling; as, to work annoy.

annoyance.c: Annoyance An*noy"ance (?), n. [OF. anoiance, anuiance.] 1. The act of annoying, or the state of being annoyed; molestation; vexation; annoy.

annoyer.c: Annoyer An*noy"er (?), n. One who, or that which, annoys.

annoying.c: Annoying An*noy"ing, a. That annoys; molesting; vexatious. -- An*noy"ing*ly, adv.

annoyous.c: Annoyous An*noy"ous (?), a. [OF. enuius, anoios.] Troublesome; annoying. [Obs.] Chaucer.

annual.c: Annual An"nu*al (?; 135), a. [OE. annuel, F. annuel, fr. L. annualis, fr. annus year. Cf. Annals.] 1. Of or pertaining to a year; returning every year; coming or happening once in the year; yearly.
Annual An"nu*al, n. 1. A thing happening or returning yearly; esp. a literary work published once a year.

annualist.c: Annualist An"nu*al*ist, n. One who writes for, or who edits, an annual. [R.]

annually.c: Annually An"nu*al*ly, adv. Yearly; year by year.

annuary.c: Annuary An"nu*a*ry (?), a. [Cf. F. annuaire.] Annual. [Obs.] -- n. A yearbook.

annueler.c: Annueler An"nu*el*er (?), n. A priest employed in saying annuals, or anniversary Masses. [Obs.] Chaucer.

annuent.c: Annuent An"nu*ent (?), a. [L. annuens, p. pr. of annuere; ad + nuere to nod.] Nodding; as, annuent muscles (used in nodding).

annuitant.c: Annuitant An*nu"i*tant (?), n. [See Annuity.] One who receives, or its entitled to receive, an annuity. Lamb.

annuity.c: Annuity An*nu"i*ty (?), n.; pl. Annuities (?). [LL. annuitas, fr. L. annus year: cf. F. annuité.] A sum of money, payable yearly, to continue for a given number of years, for life, or forever; an annual allowance.

annul.c: Annul An*nul" (?), v. t. [imp. & p. p. Annulled (?); p. pr. & vb. n. Annulling.] [F. annuler, LL. annullare, annulare, fr. L. ad to + nullus none, nullum, neut., nothing. See Null, a.] 1. To reduce to nothing; to obliterate.

annular.c: Annular An"nu*lar (?), a. [L. annularis, fr. annulis ring: cf. F. annulaire.] 1. Pertaining to, or having the form of, a ring; forming a ring; ringed; ring-shaped; as, annular fibers.

annularity.c: Annularity An`nu*lar"i*ty (?), n. Annular condition or form; as, the annularity of a nebula. J. Rogers.

annularry.c: Annularry An"nu*lar*ry, adv. In an annular manner.

annulary.c: Annulary An"nu*la*ry (?), a. [L. annularis. See Annular.] Having the form of a ring; annular. Ray.

annulata.c: Annulata ‖An`nu*la"ta (?), n. pl. [Neut. pl., fr. L. annulatus ringed.] (Zool.) A class of articulate animals, nearly equivalent to Annelida, including the marine annelids, earthworms, Gephyrea, Gymnotoma, leeches, etc. See Annelida.

annulate.c: Annulate An"nu*late (?), n. (Zool.) One of the Annulata.

annulated.c: Annulated Annulate { An"nu*late, An"nu*la`ted (?) } a. [L. annulatus.] 1. Furnished with, or composed of, rings; ringed; surrounded by rings of color.

annulation.c: Annulation An`nu*la"tion (?), n. A circular or ringlike formation; a ring or belt. Nicholson.

annulet.c: Annulet An"nu*let (?), n. [Dim. of annulus.] 1. A little ring. Tennyson.

annullable.c: Annullable An*nul"la*ble (?), a. That may be Annulled.

annulment.c: Annulment An*nul"ment (?), n. [Cf. F. annulement.] The act of annulling; abolition; invalidation.

annuloid.c: Annuloid An"nu*loid (?), a. (Zool.) Of or pertaining to the Annuloida.

annuloida.c: Annuloida ‖An`nu*loid"a (?), n. pl. [NL., fr. L. annulus ring + -oid.] (Zool.) A division of the Articulata, including the annelids and allied groups; sometimes made to include also the helminths and echinoderms. [Written also Annuloidea.]

annulosa.c: Annulosa ‖An"nu*lo"sa (?), n. pl. [NL.] (Zool.) A division of the Invertebrata, nearly equivalent to the Articulata. It includes the Arthoropoda and Anarthropoda. By some Zoologists it is applied to the former only.

annulosan.c: Annulosan An`nu*lo"san (?), n. (Zool.) One of the Annulosa.

annulose.c: Annulose An"nu*lose` (?; 277), a. [L. annulus ring.] 1. Furnished with, or composed of, rings or ringlike segments; ringed.

annulus.c: Annulus ‖An"nu*lus (?), n.; pl. Annuli (?). [L.] 1. A ring; a ringlike part or space.

annumerate.c: Annumerate An*nu"mer*ate (?), v. t. [L. annumeratus, p. p. of annumerare. See Numerate.] To add on; to count in. [Obs.] Wollaston.

annumeration.c: Annumeration An*nu`mer*a"tion (?), n. [L. annumeratio.] Addition to a former number. [Obs.] Sir T. Browne.

annunciable.c: Annunciable An*nun"ci*a*ble (?), a. That may be announced or declared; declarable. [R.]

annunciate.c: Annunciate An*nun"ci*ate (?), v. t. [imp. & p. p. Annunciated; p. pr. & vb. n. Annunciating.] [L. annuntiare. See Announce.] To announce.
Annunciate An*nun"ci*ate (?), p. p. & a. Foretold; preannounced. [Obs.] Chaucer.

annunciation.c: Annunciation An*nun`ci*a"tion (?; 277), n. [L. annuntiatio: cf. F. annonciation.] 1. The act of announcing; announcement; proclamation; as, the annunciation of peace.
Annunciation lily An*nun`ci*a"tion lil"y (?). (Bot.) The common white lily (Lilium candidum). So called because it is usually introduced by painters in pictures of the Annunciation.

annunciative.c: Annunciative An*nun"ci*a*tive (?), a. Pertaining to annunciation; announcing. [R.] Dr. H. More.

annunciator.c: Annunciator An*nun"ci*a`tor (?), n. [L. annuntiator.] 1. One who announces. Specifically: An officer in the church of Constantinople, whose business it was to inform the people of the festivals to be celebrated.

annunciatory.c: Annunciatory An*nun"ci*a*to*ry (?), a. Pertaining to, or containing, announcement; making known. [R.]

anoa.c: Anoa ‖A*noa" (?), n. [Native name.] (Zool.) A small wild ox of Celebes (Anoa depressicornis), allied to the buffalo, but having long nearly straight horns.

anode.c: Anode An"ode (?), n. [Gr.? up +? way.] (Elec.) The positive pole of an electric battery, or more strictly the electrode by which the current enters the electrolyte on its way to the other pole; -- opposed to cathode.

anodon.c: Anodon ‖An"o*don (?), n. [NL., fr. Gr.? toothless; 'an priv. +?,?, a tooth.] (Zool.) A genus of fresh-water bivalves, having no teeth at the hinge. [Written also Anodonta.]

anodyne.c: Anodyne An"o*dyne (ăn"o*dīn), a. [L. anodynus, Gr.? free from pain, stilling pain; 'an priv. +? pain: cf. F. anodin.] Serving to assuage pain; soothing.
Anodyne An"o*dyne, n. [L. anodynon. See Anodyne, a.] Any medicine which allays pain, as an opiate or narcotic; anything that soothes disturbed feelings.

anoetic.c: Anoetic An`o*et"ic (?), a. [Gr.? unthinkable;? priv. +? perceptible, thinkable.] 1. Unthinkable. [Rare]

anoil.c: Anoil A*noil" (?), v. t. [OF. enoilier.] To anoint with oil. [Obs.] Holinshed.

anoint.c: Anoint A*noint" (ȧ*noint"), v. t. [imp. & p. p. Anointed; p. pr. & vb. n. Anointing.] [OF. enoint, p. p. of enoindre, fr. L. inungere; in + ungere, unguere, to smear, anoint. See Ointment, Unguent.] 1. To smear or rub over with oil or an unctuous substance; also, to spread over, as oil.

anointment.c: anointment a*noint"ment (ȧ*noint"meint), n. The act of anointing, or state of being anointed; also, an ointment. Milton.

anolis.c: Anolis ‖A*no"lis (?), prop. n. [In the Antilles, anoli, anoalli, a lizard.] (Zool.) A genus of lizards which belong to the family Iguanidæ. They take the place in the New World of the chameleons in the Old, and in America are often called chameleons.

anomalipede.c: Anomalipede Anomaliped { A*nom"a*li*ped (?)(#), A*nom"a*li*pede (?), } a. [L. anomalus irregular + pes, pedis, foot.] Having anomalous feet.

anomaliped.c: Anomaliped A*nom"a*li*ped, n. (Zool.) One of a group of perching birds, having the middle toe more or less united to the outer and inner ones.

anomalism.c: Anomalism A*nom"a*lism (?), n. An anomaly; a deviation from rule. Hooker.

anomalistical.c: Anomalistical Anomalistic { A*nom`a*lis"tic (?), A*nom`a*lis"tic*al (?), } a. [Cf. F. anomalistique.] 1. Irregular; departing from common or established rules.

anomaloflorous.c: Anomaloflorous A*nom`a*lo*flo"rous (?), a. [L. anomalus irregular + flos, floris, flower.] (Bot.) Having anomalous flowers.

anomalous.c: Anomalous A*nom"a*lous (?), a. [L. anomalus, Gr.? uneven, irregular; 'an priv. +? even,? same. See Same, and cf. Abnormal.] Deviating from a general rule, method, or analogy; abnormal; irregular; as, an anomalous proceeding.

anomalously.c: Anomalously A*nom"a*lous*ly, adv. In an anomalous manner.

anomalousness.c: Anomalousness A*nom"a*lous*ness, n. Quality of being anomalous.

anomaly.c: Anomaly A*nom"a*ly (?), n.; pl. Anomalies (?). [L. anomalia, Gr.?. See Anomalous.] 1. Deviation from the common rule; an irregularity; anything anomalous.

anomia.c: Anomia ‖A*no"mi*a (?), n. [NL., fr. Gr.? irregular; 'a priv. + no`mos law.] (Zool.) A genus of bivalve shells, allied to the oyster, so called from their unequal valves, of which the lower is perforated for attachment.

anomophyllous.c: Anomophyllous An`o*moph"yl*lous (?), a. [Gr.? irregular +? leaf.] (Bot.) Having leaves irregularly placed.

anomoura.c: Anomoura Anomura { ‖An`o*mu"ra (?), ‖An`o*mou"ra (?), } n. pl. [NL., fr. Gr.? lawless + o'yra` tail.] (Zool.) A group of decapod Crustacea, of which the hermit crab in an example.

anomuran.c: Anomuran Anomural { An`o*mu"ral (?), An`o*mu"ran (?), } a. Irregular in the character of the tail or abdomen; as, the anomural crustaceans. [Written also anomoural, anomouran.]
Anomuran An`o*mu"ran, n. (Zool.) One of the Anomura.

anomy.c: Anomy An"o*my (?), n. [Gr.?. See Anomia.] Disregard or violation of law. [R.] Glanvill.

anon.c: Anon A*non" (?), adv. [OE. anoon, anon, anan, lit., in one (moment), fr. AS. on in + ān one. See On and One.] 1. Straightway; at once. [Obs.]

anona.c: Anona ‖A*no"na, n. [NL. Cf. Ananas.] (Bot.) A genus of tropical or subtropical plants of the natural order Anonaceæ, including the soursop.

anonaceous.c: Anonaceous An`o*na"ceous, a. Pertaining to the order of plants including the soursop, custard apple, etc.

anonym.c: Anonym An"o*nym (?), n. [F. anonyme. See Anonymous.] 1. One who is anonymous; also sometimes used for “pseudonym.”

anonymity.c: Anonymity An`o*nym"i*ty, n. The quality or state of being anonymous; anonymousness; also, that which anonymous. [R.]

anonymous.c: Anonymous A*non"y*mous, a. [Gr.? without name; 'an priv. +?, Eol. for? name. See Name.] Nameless; of unknown name; also, of unknown or unavowed authorship; as, an anonymous benefactor; an anonymous pamphlet or letter.

anonymously.c: Anonymously A*non"y*mous*ly (ȧ*nŏn"ĭ*mŭs*ly̆), adv. In an anonymous manner; without a name. Swift.

anonymousness.c: Anonymousness A*non"y*mous*ness, n. The state or quality of being anonymous. Coleridge.

anopheles.c: Anopheles ‖A*noph"e*les (ȧ*nŏf"e*lēz), n. [NL., fr. Gr. 'anwfelh`s useless, hurtful.] (Zool.) A genus of mosquitoes which are secondary hosts of the malaria parasites, and whose bite is the usual, if not the only, means of infecting human beings with malaria. Several species are found in the United States. They may be distinguished from the ordinary mosquitoes of the genus Culex by the long slender palpi, nearly equaling the beak in length, while those of the female Culex are very short. They also assume different positions when resting, Culex usually holding the body parallel to the surface on which it rests and keeping the head and beak bent at an angle, while Anopheles holds the body at an angle with the surface and the head and beak in line with it. Unless they become themselves infected by previously biting a subject affected with malaria, the insects cannot transmit the disease.

anophyte.c: Anophyte An"o*phyte (ăn"o*fīt), n. [Gr. 'a`nw upward (fr. 'ana` up) + fyto`n a plant, fy`ein to grow.] (Bot.) A moss or mosslike plant which cellular stems, having usually an upward growth and distinct leaves.

anopla.c: Anopla ‖An"o*pla (ăn"ŏ*plȧ), n. pl. [NL., fr. Gr. 'a`noplos unarmed.] (Zool.) One of the two orders of Nemerteans. See Nemertina.

anoplotherium.c: Anoplotherium Anoplothere An*op"lo*there (ăn*ŏp"lo*thēr), ‖An`o*plo*the"ri*um (ăn`o*plo*thē"rĭ*ŭm), n. [From Gr. 'a`noplos unarmed ('an priv. + 'o`plon an implement, weapon) + qhri`on beast.] (Paleon.) A genus of extinct quadrupeds of the order Ungulata, whose were first found in the gypsum quarries near Paris; characterized by the shortness and feebleness of their canine teeth (whence the name).

anoplura.c: Anoplura ‖An`o*plu"ra (ăn`o*plū"rȧ), n. pl. [NL., fr. Gr. 'an priv. + 'o`plon weapon, sting + o'yra` tail.] (Zool.) A group of insects which includes the lice.

anopsy.c: anopsy anopsia anopia { ‖a*nop"si*a (ȧ*nŏp"sĭ*ȧ), an"op`sy (ăn"ŏp`sy̆), an*op"i*a } a. [Gr. 'an priv. + 'o`psis sight.] (Med.) Defect or absence of sight; blindness.

anorexia.c: anorexia anorexy { ‖an`o*rex"i*a (ăn`o*rĕks"ĭ*ȧ), an"o*rex`y (ăn"o*rĕks`y̆) } n. [Gr. 'anorexi`a; 'an priv. + 'o`rexis desire, appetite, 'ore`gein desire.] (Med.) Loss of appetite for food. Coxe.

anormal.c: Anormal A*nor"mal (?), a. [F. anormal. See Abnormal, Normal.] Not according to rule; abnormal. [Obs.]

anorn.c: Anorn A*norn (?), v. t. [OF. aörner, aöurner, fr. L. adornare to adorn. The form a-ourne was corrupted into anourne.] To adorn. [Obs.] Bp. Watson.

anorthic.c: Anorthic A*nor"thic (?), a. [See Anorthite.] (Min.) Having unequal oblique axes; as, anorthic crystals.

anorthite.c: Anorthite A*nor"thite (?), n. [Gr. 'an priv. + 'orqo`s straight ('orqh` sc. gwni`a right angle); not in a right angle.] A mineral of the feldspar family, commonly occurring in small glassy crystals, also a constituent of some igneous rocks. It is a lime feldspar. See Feldspar.

anorthoclase.c: Anorthoclase A*nor"tho*clase (?), n. [Gr. 'an priv. + orthoclase.] (Min.) A feldspar closely related to orthoclase, but triclinic. It is chiefly a silicate of sodium, potassium, and aluminium. Sp. gr., 2.57 -- 2.60.

anorthopia.c: anorthopia ‖an`or*tho"pi*a (ăn`ŏr*thō"pĭ*ȧ), n. [NL., fr. Gr. 'an priv. + ortho- + Gr. 'w`ps, 'wpo`s, the eye.] (Med.) Distorted vision, in which straight lines appear bent. AS

anorthoscope.c: Anorthoscope A*nor"tho*scope (?), n. [Gr. 'an priv. + 'orqo`s straight + -scope.] (Physics) An optical toy for producing amusing figures or pictures by means of two revolving disks, on one of which distorted figures are painted.

anorthosite.c: Anorthosite A*nor"tho*site (?), n. [F. anorthose triclinic feldspar (fr. Gr. 'an priv. + 'orqo`s straight) + -ite.] (Petrol.) A granular igneous rock composed almost exclusively of a soda-lime feldspar, usually labradorite.

anosmia.c: anosmia ‖a*nos"mi*a (ăn*ŏz"me*ȧ), n. [NL., fr. Gr. 'an priv. + 'osmh` smell.] (Med.) Loss of the sense of smell. AS

another.c: another an*oth"er (ăn*ŭth"ẽr), pron. & a. [An a, one + other.] 1. One more, in addition to a former number; a second or additional one, similar in likeness or in effect.

anothergaines.c: Another-gaines An*oth"er-gaines` (?), a. [Corrupted fr. another-gates.] Of another kind. [Obs.] Sir P. Sidney.

anothergates.c: Another-gates An*oth"er-gates` (?), a. [Another + gate, or gait, way. Cf. Algates.] Of another sort. [Obs.] “Another-gates adventure.” Hudibras.

anotherguess.c: Another-guess An*oth"er-guess (?), a. [Corrupted fr. another-gates.] Of another sort. [Archaic]

anoxaemia.c: anoxaemia anoxemia ‖an`ox*ae"mi*a, an`ox*e"mi*a (ăn`ŏks*ē"mĭ*ȧ), n. [NL.; Gr. 'an priv. + oxygen + Gr. a'i^ma blood.] (Med.) A former term used to refer to an abnormal condition due to deficient oxygenation of the arterial blood, as in balloon sickness, mountain sickness; now the term is replaced by the term hypoxemia. -- An`ox*ae"mic, An`ox*e"mic (ăn`ŏks*ē"mĭk), a.

anoxia.c: anoxia an`ox"i*a (ăn*ŏks"ĭ*ȧ), n. [NL.; Gr. 'an priv. + oxygen.] 1. (Med.) A physiological state in which insufficient oxygen reaches the tissues of the body, especially when of sufficient severity to cause permanent damage; severe hypoxia.

ansa.c: Ansa ‖An"sa (ăn"sȧ), n.; pl. Ansæ (ăn"sǣ). [L., a handle.] (Astron.) A name given to either of the projecting ends of Saturn's ring.

ansated.c: Ansated An"sa*ted (?), a. [L. ansatus, fr. ansa a handle.] Having a handle. Johnson.

anserated.c: Anserated An"ser*a`ted (?), a. (Her.) Having the extremities terminate in the heads of eagles, lions, etc.; as, an anserated cross.

anseres.c: Anseres ‖An"se*res (?), n. pl. [L., geese.] (Zool.) A Linnæan order of aquatic birds swimming by means of webbed feet, as the duck, or of lobed feet, as the grebe. In this order were included the geese, ducks, auks, divers, gulls, petrels, etc.

anseriformes.c: Anseriformes ‖An`se*ri*for"mes (?), n. pl. (Zool.) A division of birds including the geese, ducks, and closely allied forms.

anserine.c: Anserine An"ser*ine (?), a. [L. anserinus, fr. anser a goose.] 1. Pertaining to, or resembling, a goose, or the skin of a goose.

anserous.c: Anserous An"ser*ous (?), a. [L. anser a goose.] Resembling a goose; silly; simple. Sydney Smith.

answer.c: Answer An"swer (ăn"sẽr), v. t. [imp. & p. p. Answered (ăn"sẽrd); p. pr. & vb. n. Answering.] [OE. andswerien, AS. andswerian, andswarian, to answer, fr. andswaru, n., answer. See Answer, n.] 1. To speak in defense against; to reply to in defense; as, to answer a charge; to answer an accusation.
Answer An"swer, v. i. 1. To speak or write by way of return (originally, to a charge), or in reply; to make response.
Answer An"swer, n. [OE. andsware, AS. andswaru; and against + swerian to swear. √177, 196. See Anti-, and Swear, and cf. 1st un-.] 1. A reply to a charge; a defense.

answerable.c: Answerable An"swer*a*ble (?), a. 1. Obliged to answer; liable to be called to account; liable to pay, indemnify, or make good; accountable; amenable; responsible; as, an agent is answerable to his principal; to be answerable for a debt, or for damages.

answerableness.c: Answerableness An"swer*a*ble*ness, n. The quality of being answerable, liable, responsible, or correspondent.

answerably.c: Answerably An"swer*a*bly (?), adv. In an answerable manner; in due proportion or correspondence; suitably.

answerless.c: Answerless An"swer*less (?), a. Having no answer, or impossible to be answered. Byron.

ant.c: An't An't (?). A contraction for are and am not; also used for is not; -- now usually written ain't. [Colloq. & illiterate speech.]

-ant -ant. [F. -ant, fr. L. -antem or -entem, the pr. p. ending; also sometimes directly from L. -antem.] A suffix sometimes marking the agent for action; as, merchant, covenant, servant, pleasant, etc. Cf. -ent.

Ant Ant (?), n. [OE. ante, amete, emete, AS. æmete akin to G. ameise. Cf. Emmet.] (Zool.) A hymenopterous insect of the Linnæan genus Formica, which is now made a family of several genera; an emmet; a pismire.
Ant bird Ant" bird (?), (Zool.) See Ant bird, under Ant, n.
Ant cow Ant cow. (Zool.) Any aphid from which ants obtain honeydew. The plural form is ant cattle.
Ant egg Ant" egg` (?). One of the small white egg-shaped pupæ or cocoons of the ant, often seen in or about ant-hills, and popularly supposed to be eggs.

Ant thrush Ant" thrush` (?). (Zool.) (a) One of several species of tropical birds, of the Old World, of the genus Pitta, somewhat resembling the thrushes, and feeding chiefly on ants. (b) See Ant bird, under Ant.

anta.c: Anta ‖An"ta (?), n.; pl. Antæ (?). [L.] (Arch.) A species of pier produced by thickening a wall at its termination, treated architecturally as a pilaster, with capital and base.

antacid.c: antacid antiacid ‖ant*ac"id (ănt*ăs"ĭd), an*ti*ac"id (ăn*te*ăs"ĭd), n. [Pref. anti- + acid.] (Med.) A remedy for neutralizing acidity, especially of the stomach, as an alkali or absorbent. -- a. Counteractive of acidity.

antacrid.c: Antacrid Ant*ac"rid (?), a. [Pref. anti- + acrid.] Corrective of acrimony of the humors.

antaean.c: Antaean An*tae"an (?), a. [Gr.?.] Pertaining to Antaeus, a giant athlete slain by Hercules.

antagonism.c: antagonism an*tag"o*nism (ăn*tăg"o*nĭz'm), n. [Gr. 'antagw`nisma, fr. 'antagwni`zesqai to struggle against; 'anti` against + 'agwni`zesqai to contend or struggle, 'agw`n contest: cf. F. antagonisme. See Agony.] Opposition of action; counteraction or contrariety of things or principles.

antagonist.c: antagonist an*tag"o*nist (ăn*tăg"o*nĭst), n. [L. antagonista, Gr. 'antagwnisth`s; 'anti` against + 'agwnisth`s combatant, champion, fr. 'agwni`zesqai: cf. F. antagoniste. See Antagonism.] 1. One who contends with another, especially in combat; an adversary; an opponent.
Antagonist An*tag"o*nist, a. Antagonistic; opposing; counteracting; as, antagonist schools of philosophy.

antagonistic.c: Antagonistic Antagonistical { An*tag`o*nis"tic (?), An*tag`o*nis"tic*al (?), } a. Opposing in combat, combating; contending or acting against; as, antagonistic forces. -- An*tag`o*nis"tic*al*ly, adv.

antagonize.c: Antagonize An*tag"o*nize (?), v. t. [imp. & p. p. Antagonized (?); p. pr. & vb. n. Antagonozing.] [Gr.?. See Antagonism.] To contend with; to oppose actively; to counteract.
Antagonize An*tag"o*nize, v. i. To act in opposition.

antagony.c: Antagony An*tag"o*ny (?), n. [Gr.?; 'anti` +? contest: cf. F. (16th century) antagonie. See Antagonism.] Contest; opposition; antagonism. [Obs.]

antalgic.c: antalgic an*tal"gic (ăn*tăl"jĭk), a. [Pref. anti- + Gr. 'a`lgos pain: cf. F. antalgique.] (Med.) Alleviating pain. -- n. A medicine to alleviate pain; an analgesic. [R.]

antalkaline.c: Antalkaline Antalkali Ant*al"ka*li (?; 277), Ant*al"ka*line (?), n. [Pref. anti- + alkali.] Anything that neutralizes, or that counteracts an alkaline tendency in the system. Hooper.
Antalkaline Ant*al"ka*line, a. Of power to counteract alkalies.

antambulacral.c: Antambulacral Ant*am`bu*la"cral (ănt*ăm`bu*lā"krail), a. (Zool.) Away from the ambulacral region.

antanaclasis.c: Antanaclasis ‖Ant`an*a*cla"sis (?), n. [Gr.?; 'anti`/ + 'ana`klasis a bending back and breaking. See Anaclastic.] (Rhet.) (a) A figure which consists in repeating the same word in a different sense; as, Learn some craft when young, that when old you may live without craft. (b) A repetition of words beginning a sentence, after a long parenthesis; as, Shall that heart (which not only feels them, but which has all motions of life placed in them), shall that heart, etc.

antanagoge.c: Antanagoge ‖Ant`an*a*go"ge (?), n. [Pref. anti- + anagoge.] (Rhet.) A figure which consists in answering the charge of an adversary, by a counter charge.

antaphroditic.c: antaphroditic ant`aph*ro*dit"ic (ănt`ăf*ro*dĭt"ĭk), a. [Pref. anti- + Gr. 'Afrodi`th Aphrodite: cf. F. antaphroditique.] (Med.) 1. Antaphrodisiac. AS

antapoplectic.c: Antapoplectic Ant`ap*o*plec"tic (ănt`ăp*o*plĕk"tĭk), a. [Pref. anti- + apoplectic.] (Med.) Alleviating apoplexy. -- n. A medicine used for alleviating apoplexy. [Obs.]

antarchism.c: Antarchism Ant*ar"chism (?), n. [Pref. anti- + Gr.? government.] Opposition to government in general. [R.]

antarchist.c: Antarchist Ant*ar"chist (?), n. One who opposes all government. [R.]

antarchistical.c: Antarchistical Antarchistic { Ant`ar*chis"tic (?), Ant`ar*chis"tic*al (?), } a. Opposed to all human government. [R.]

antarctic.c: Antarctic Ant*arc"tic (?), a. [OE. antartik, OF. antartique, F. antarctique, L. antarcticus, fr. Gr.?; 'anti` + 'a`rktos bear. See Arctic.] Opposite to the northern or arctic pole; relating to the southern pole or to the region near it, and applied especially to a circle, distant from the pole 23° 28−. Thus we say the antarctic pole, circle, ocean, region, current, etc.

antares.c: Antares ‖An*ta"res (?), n. [Gr.?;? similar to +? Mars. It was thought to resemble Mars in color.] The principal star in Scorpio: -- called also the Scorpion's Heart.

antarthritic.c: antarthritic antiarthritic ant`ar*thrit"ic(ănt`är*thrĭt"ĭk), ant`i*ar*thrit"ic (ănt`e*är*thrĭt"ĭk), a. [Pref. anti- + arthritic.] (Med.) Alleviating arthritis. -- n. A remedy for alleviating arthritis. AS

antasthmatic.c: antasthmatic ant`asth*mat"ic (ănt`ăz*măt"ĭk; see Asthma; 277), a. [Pref. anti- + asthmatic.] (Med.) Opposing, or fitted to relieve, asthma. -- n. A remedy for asthma. AS
Antasthmatic Ant`asth*mat"ic (? or?; see Asthma; 277), a. [Pref. anti- + asthmatic.] (Med.) Opposing, or fitted to relieve, asthma. -- n. A remedy for asthma.

antbear.c: Ant-bear Ant"-bear` (?), n. (Zool.) An edentate animal of tropical America (the Tamanoir), living on ants. It belongs to the genus Myrmecophaga.

antcattle.c: Ant-cattle Ant"-cat`tle (?), n. pl. (Zool.) Various kinds of plant lice or aphids tended by ants for the sake of the honeydew which they secrete; plural of ant cow. See Aphips.

ante.c: Ante- An"te- (ăn"te-). A Latin preposition and prefix; akin to Gr. 'anti`, Skr. anti, Goth. and-, anda- (only in comp.), AS. and-, ond-, (only in comp.: cf. Answer, Along), G. ant-, ent- (in comp.). The Latin ante is generally used in the sense of before, in regard to position, order, or time, and the Gr. 'anti` in that of opposite, or in the place of.
Ante An"te, n. (Poker Playing) Each player's stake, which is put into the pool before (ante) the game begins.
Ante An"te, v. t. & i. To put up (an ante).ante up. -->
Ante mortem ‖An`te mor"tem (?). [L.] Before death; -- generally used adjectively; as, an ante-mortem statement; ante-mortem examination.

anteal.c: Anteal An"te*al (?), a. [antea, ante, before. Cf. Ancient.] Being before, or in front. [R.] J. Fleming.

anteater.c: Ant-eater Ant"-eat`er (?), n. (Zool.) One of several species of edentates and monotremes that feed upon ants. See Ant-bear, Pangolin, Aard-vark, and Echidna.

antecedaneous.c: Antecedaneous An`te*ce*da"ne*ous (?), a. [See Antecede.] Antecedent; preceding in time. “Capable of antecedaneous proof.” Barrow.

antecede.c: Antecede An`te*cede" (?), v. t. & i. [L. antecedere; ante + cedere to go. See Cede.] To go before in time or place; to precede; to surpass. Sir M. Hale.

antecedence.c: Antecedence An`te*ced"ence (?), n. 1. The act or state of going before in time; precedence. H. Spenser.

antecedency.c: Antecedency An`te*ced"en*cy (?), n. The state or condition of being antecedent; priority. Fothherby.

antecedent.c: Antecedent An`te*ced"ent (?), a. [L. antecedens, -entis, p. pr. of antecedere: cf. F. antécédent.] 1. Going before in time; prior; anterior; preceding; as, an event antecedent to the Deluge; an antecedent cause.
Antecedent An`te*ced"ent, n. [Cf. F. antécédent.] 1. That which goes before in time; that which precedes. South.

antecedently.c: Antecedently An`te*ced"ent*ly (?), adv. Previously; before in time; at a time preceding; as, antecedently to conversion. Barrow.

antecessor.c: Antecessor An`te*ces"sor (?), n. [L., fr. antecedere, antecessum. See Antecede, Ancestor.] 1. One who goes before; a predecessor.

antechamber.c: Antechamber An"te*cham`ber (?), n. [Cf. F. antichambre.] 1. A chamber or apartment before the chief apartment and leading into it, in which persons wait for audience; an outer chamber. See Lobby.

antechapel.c: Antechapel An"te*chap`el (?), n. The outer part of the west end of a collegiate or other chapel. Shipley.

antechoir.c: Antechoir An"te*choir` (?), n. (Arch.) (a) A space inclosed or reserved at the entrance to the choir, for the clergy and choristers. (b) Where a choir is divided, as in some Spanish churches, that division of it which is the farther from the sanctuary.

antecommunion.c: Antecommunion An`te*com*mun"ion (?), n. A name given to that part of the Anglican liturgy for the communion, which precedes the consecration of the elements.

antecursor.c: Antecursor An`te*cur"sor (?), n. [L., fr. antecurrere to run before; ante + currere to run.] A forerunner; a precursor. [Obs.]

antedate.c: Antedate An"te*date` (ăn`te*dāt`), n. 1. Prior date; a date antecedent to another which is the actual date.

Antedate An"te*date` (ăn`te*dāt`), v. t. [imp. & p. p. Antedated; p. pr. & vb. n. Antedating.] 1. To date before the true time; to assign to an earlier date;; thus, to antedate a deed or a bond is to give it a date anterior to the true time of its execution.

antediluvial.c: Antediluvial An`te*di*lu"vi*al (ăn`te*dĭ*lū"vĭ*ail), a. [Pref. ante- + diluvial.] Before the flood, or Deluge, in Noah's time.

antediluvian.c: antediluvian an`te*di*lu"vi*an (ăn`te*dĭ*lū"vĭ*ain), a. Of or relating to the period before the Deluge in Noah's time; hence, antiquated; as, an antediluvian vehicle. -- n. One who lived before the Deluge.

antefact.c: antefact an"te*fact` (ăn`te*făkt`), n. Something done before another act. [Obs.]

antefix.c: Antefix An"te*fix` (?), n.; pl. E. Antefixes (?); L. Antefixa (?). [L. ante + fixus fixed.] (Arch.) (a) An ornament fixed upon a frieze. (b) An ornament at the eaves, concealing the ends of the joint tiles of the roof. (c) An ornament of the cymatium of a classic cornice, sometimes pierced for the escape of water.

anteflexion.c: anteflexion an`te*flex"ion (ăn`te*flĕk"shŭn), n. (Med.) A displacement forward of an organ, esp. the uterus, in such manner that its axis is bent upon itself. T. G. Thomas. AS

antelope.c: Antelope An"te*lope (ăn"te*lōp), n. [OF. antelop, F. antilope, from Gr. 'anqo`lops, -lopos, Eustathius, “Hexaëm.,” p. 36, the origin of which is unknown.] (Zool.) One of a group of ruminant quadrupeds, intermediate between the deer and the goat. The horns are usually annulated, or ringed. There are many species in Africa and Asia.

antelucan.c: Antelucan An`te*lu"can (?), a. [L. antelucanus; ante + lux light.] Held or being before light; -- a word applied to assemblies of Christians, in ancient times of persecution, held before light in the morning. “Antelucan worship.” De Quincey.

antemeridian.c: Antemeridian An`te*me*rid"i*an (?), a. [L. antemeridianus; ante + meridianus belonging to midday or noon. See Meridian.] Being before noon; in or pertaining to the forenoon. (Abbrev. a. m.)

antemetic.c: Antemetic Ant`e*met"ic (?), a. [Pref. anti- + emetic.] (Med.) Tending to check vomiting. -- n. A remedy to check or allay vomiting.

antemosaic.c: Antemosaic An`te*mo*sa"ic (?), a. Being before the time of Moses.

antemundane.c: Antemundane An`te*mun"dane (?), a. Being or occurring before the creation of the world. Young.

antemural.c: Antemural An`te*mu"ral (?), n. [L. antemurale: ante + murus wall. See Mural.] An outwork of a strong, high wall, with turrets, in front of the gateway (as of an old castle), for defending the entrance.

antenicene.c: Antenicene An`te*ni"cene (?), a. [L.] Of or in the Christian church or era, anterior to the first council of Nice, held a. d. 325; as, antenicene faith.

antenna.c: Antenna An*ten"na (?), n.; pl. Antennæ (?). [L. antenna sail-yard; NL., a feeler, horn of an insect.] 1. (Zool.) A movable, articulated organ of sensation, attached to the heads of insects and Crustacea. There are two in the former, and usually four in the latter. They are used as organs of touch, and in some species of Crustacea the cavity of the ear is situated near the basal joint. In insects, they are popularly called horns, and also feelers. The term in also applied to similar organs on the heads of other arthropods and of annelids.

antennal.c: Antennal An*ten"nal (?), a. (Zool.) Belonging to the antennæ. Owen.

antenniferous.c: Antenniferous An`ten*nif"er*ous (?), a. [Antenna + -ferous.] (Zool.) Bearing or having antennæ.

antennule.c: Antennule An*ten"nule (?), n. [Dim. of antenna.] (Zool.) A small antenna; -- applied to the smaller pair of antennæ or feelers of Crustacea.

antenumber.c: Antenumber An`te*num"ber (?), n. A number that precedes another. [R.] Bacon.

antenuptial.c: Antenuptial An`te*nup"tial (?), a. Preceding marriage; as, an antenuptial agreement. Kent.

anteorbital.c: Anteorbital An`te*or"bit*al (?), a. & n. (Anat.) Same as Antorbital.

antepaschal.c: Antepaschal An`te*pas"chal (?), a. Pertaining to the time before the Passover, or before Easter.

antepast.c: Antepast An"te*past (?), n. [Pref. ante- + L. pastus pasture, food. Cf. Repast.] A foretaste.

antependium.c: Antependium ‖An`te*pen"di*um (?), n. [LL., fr. L. ante + pendere to hang.] (Eccl.) The hangings or screen in front of the altar; an altar cloth; the frontal. Smollett.

antepenultima.c: Antepenultima Antepenult { An`te*pe"nult (?), ‖An`te*pe*nult"i*ma (?), } n. [L. antepaenultima (sc. syllaba) antepenultimate; ante before + paenultimus the last but one; paene almost + ultimus last.] (Pros.) The last syllable of a word except two, as -syl- in monosyllable.

antepenultimate.c: Antepenultimate An`te*pe*nult"i*mate (?), a. Of or pertaining to the last syllable but two. -- n. The antepenult.

antephialtic.c: Antephialtic Ant`eph*i*al"tic (?), a. [Pref. anti- + Gr.? nightmare.] (Med.) Good against nightmare. -- n. A remedy nightmare. Dunglison.

antepileptic.c: Antepileptic Ant`ep*i*lep"tic (?), a. [Pref. anti- + epileptic.] (Med.) Good against epilepsy. -- n. A medicine for epilepsy.

antepone.c: Antepone An"te*pone (?), v. t. [L. anteponere.] To put before; to prefer. [Obs.] Bailey.

anteport.c: Anteport An"te*port (?), n. [Cf. LL. anteporta.] An outer port, gate, or door.

anteportico.c: Anteportico An`te*por"ti*co (?), n. An outer porch or vestibule.

anteposition.c: Anteposition An`te*po*si"tion (?), n. [Cf. LL. antepositio. See Position.] (Gram.) The placing of a before another, which, by ordinary rules, ought to follow it.

antepredicament.c: Antepredicament An`te*pre*dic"a*ment (?), n. (Logic) A prerequisite to a clear understanding of the predicaments and categories, such as definitions of common terms. Chambers.

anterior.c: Anterior An*te"ri*or (?), a. [L. anterior, comp. of ante before.] 1. Before in time; antecedent.

anteriority.c: Anteriority An*te`ri*or"i*ty (?), n. [LL. anterioritas.] The state of being anterior or preceding in time or in situation; priority. Pope.

anteriorly.c: Anteriorly An*te"ri*or*ly (?), adv. In an anterior manner; before.

anteroom.c: Anteroom An"te*room (?), n. A room before, or forming an entrance to, another; a waiting room.

antero.c: Antero- An"te*ro- (?). A combining form meaning anterior, front; as, antero-posterior, front and back; antero-lateral, front side, anterior and at the side.

antes.c: Antes An"tes (?), n. pl. Antæ. See Anta.

antestature.c: Antestature An`te*stat"ure (?), n. (Fort.) A small intrenchment or work of palisades, or of sacks of earth.

antestomach.c: Antestomach An"te*stom`ach (?), n. A cavity which leads into the stomach, as in birds. Ray.

antetemple.c: Antetemple An"te*tem`ple (?), n. The portico, or narthex in an ancient temple or church.

anteversion.c: Anteversion An`te*ver"sion (?), n. [Pref. ante- + L. vertere, versum, to turn.] (Med.) A displacement of an organ, esp. of the uterus, in such manner that its whole axis is directed further forward than usual.

antevert.c: Antevert An`te*vert" (?), v. t. [L. antevertere; ante + vertere to turn.] 1. To prevent. [Obs.] Bp. Hall.

anthelion.c: Anthelion Ant*hel"ion (?; 277, 106), n.; pl. Anthelia (?). [Pref. anti + Gr.? sun.] (Meteor.) A halo opposite the sun, consisting of a colored ring or rings around the shadow of the spectator's own head, as projected on a cloud or on an opposite fog bank.

anthelmintic.c: Anthelmintic anthelminthic anthelminthic, An`thel*min"tic (ăn`thĕl*mĭn"tĭk), a. [Pref. anti- + Gr. "e`lmins, -inqos, worm, esp. a tapeworm, or mawworm. See also helminth] (Med.) capable of expelling or destroying parasitic worms. -- n. An anthelmintic remedy. [Written also anthelminthic.]

anthem.c: Anthem An"them (ăn"thĕm), n. [OE. antym, antefne, AS. antefen, fr. LL. antiphona, fr. Gr. 'anti`fwna, neut. pl. of 'anti`fwnon antiphon, or anthem, n. neut., from 'anti`fwnos sounding contrary, returning a sound; 'anti` over against + fwnh` sound, voice: the anthem being sung by the choristers alternately, one half-choir answering the other: cf. OF. anthaine, anteine, antieune, F. antienne. See Antiphon.] 1. Formerly, a hymn sung in alternate parts, in present usage, a selection from the Psalms, or other parts of the Scriptures or the liturgy, set to sacred music.
Anthem An"them, v. t. To celebrate with anthems. [Poet.]

anthemion.c: Anthemion ‖ An*the"mi*on (?), [ fr. Gr. 'anqemi`s flower.] A floral ornament. See Palmette.

anthemis.c: Anthemis ‖An"the*mis (?), n. [Gr. 'anqemi`s, equiv. to 'a`nqos flower; an herb like our chamomile.] (Bot.) Chamomile; a genus of composite, herbaceous plants.

anther.c: Anther An"ther (?), n. [F. anthère, L. anthera a medicine composed of flowers, fr. Gr.? flowery, fr. 'anqei^n to bloom, 'a`nqos flower.] (Bot.) That part of the stamen containing the pollen, or fertilizing dust, which, when mature, is emitted for the impregnation of the ovary. -- An"ther*al (?), a.

antheridium.c: Antheridium ‖An`ther*id"i*um (?), n.; pl. Antheridia (?). [Anther +? (a Gr. diminutive ending).] (Bot.) The male reproductive apparatus in the lower plants, consisting of a cell or other cavity in which spermatozoids are produced; -- called also spermary. -- An`ther*id"i*al (?), a.

antheriferous.c: Antheriferous An`ther*if"er*ous (?), a. [Anther + -ferous.] (Bot.) (a) Producing anthers, as plants. (b) Supporting anthers, as a part of a flower. Gray.

antheriform.c: Antheriform An*ther"i*form (?), a. [Anther + -form.] Shaped like an anther; anther-shaped.

antherogenous.c: Antherogenous An`ther*og"e*nous (?), a. [Anther + -genous.] (Bot.) Transformed from anthers, as the petals of a double flower.

antherozooid.c: Antherozooid Antherozoid { An`ther*o*zoid (?), An`ther*o*zoo"id (?), } n. [Gr.? flowery +? animal + -oid. See Zooid.] (Bot.) One of the mobile male reproductive bodies in the antheridia of cryptogams.

anthesis.c: Anthesis ‖An*the"sis (?), n. [Gr.? bloom, fr. 'anqei^n to bloom, 'a`nqos flower.] (Bot.) The period or state of full expansion in a flower. Gray.

anthill.c: Ant-hill Ant"-hill (?), n. (Zool.) A mound thrown up by ants or by termites in forming their nests.

anthobian.c: Anthobian An*tho"bi*an (?), n. [Gr. 'a`nqos flower + bi`os life.] (Zool.) A beetle which feeds on flowers.

anthobranchia.c: Anthobranchia ‖An`tho*bran"chi*a (?), n. pl. [NL., fr. Gr. 'a`nqos flower +? gills, n. pl.] (Zool.) A division of nudibranchiate Mollusca, in which the gills form a wreath or cluster upon the posterior part of the back. See Nudibranchiata, and Doris.

anthocarpous.c: Anthocarpous An`tho*car"pous (?), a. [Gr. 'a`nqos flower + karpo`s fruit.] (Bot.) Having some portion of the floral envelopes attached to the pericarp to form the fruit, as in the checkerberry, the mulberry, and the pineapple.

anthodium.c: Anthodium ‖An*tho"di*um (?), n. [NL., from Gr.? like flowers, flowery; 'a`nqos flower + e'i^dos form.] (Bot.) The inflorescence of a compound flower in which many florets are gathered into a involucrate head.

anthography.c: Anthography An*thog"ra*phy (?), n. [Gr. 'a`nqos flower + -graphy.] A description of flowers.

anthoid.c: Anthoid An"thoid (?), a. [Gr. 'a`nqos flower + -oid.] Resembling a flower; flowerlike.

anthokyan.c: Anthokyan An`tho*ky"an (?), n. [Gr. 'a`nqos flower + ky`anos blue.] (Chem.) The blue coloring matter of certain flowers. Same as Cyanin.

antholite.c: Antholite An"tho*lite (?), n. [Gr. 'a`nqos flower + -lite.] (Paleon.) A fossil plant, like a petrified flower.

anthological.c: Anthological An`tho*log"ic*al (?), a. Pertaining to anthology; consisting of beautiful extracts from different authors, especially the poets.

anthologist.c: Anthologist An*thol"o*gist (?), n. One who compiles an anthology.

anthology.c: Anthology An*thol"o*gy (?), n. [Gr.?, fr. 'anqolo`gos flower gathering; 'a`nqos flower + le`gein to gather.] 1. A discourse on flowers. [R.]

anthomania.c: Anthomania An`tho*ma"ni*a (?), n. [Gr. 'a`nqos flower + mani`a madness.] A extravagant fondness for flowers. [R.]

anthonys.c: Anthony's Fire An"tho*ny's Fire` (?). See Saint Anthony's Fire, under Saint.

anthophagous.c: Anthophagous An*thoph"a*gous (?), a. [Gr. 'a`nqos flower + fagei^n to eat.] (Zool.) Eating flowers; -- said of certain insects.

anthophilous.c: Anthophilous An*thoph"i*lous (?), a. [Gr. 'a`nqos flower + fi`los loving.] (Zool.) Lit., fond of flowers; hence, feeding upon, or living among, flowers.

anthophore.c: Anthophore An"tho*phore (?), n. [Gr.? bearing flowers; 'a`nqos flower +? bearing, fe`rein to bear.] (Bot.) The stipe when developed into an internode between calyx and corolla, as in the Pink family. Gray.

anthophorous.c: Anthophorous An*thoph"o*rous (?), a. Flower bearing; supporting the flower.

anthophyllite.c: Anthophyllite An*thoph"yl*lite (?), n. [NL. anthophyllum clove.] A mineral of the hornblende group, of a yellowish gray or clove brown color. -- An`tho*phyl*lit"ic (?), a.

anthorism.c: Anthorism An"tho*rism (?), n. [Gr.?;? +? to bound, define.] (Rhet.) A description or definition contrary to that which is given by the adverse party. [R.]

anthotaxy.c: Anthotaxy An"tho*tax`y (?), n. [Gr. 'a`nqos flower +? order.] (Bot.) The arrangement of flowers in a cluster; the science of the relative position of flowers; inflorescence.

anthozoa.c: Anthozoa ‖An`tho*zo"a (?), n. pl. [NL., fr. Gr. 'a`nqos flower +? animal.] (Zool.) The class of the Cœlenterata which includes the corals and sea anemones. The three principal groups or orders are Acyonaria, Actinaria, and Madreporaria.

anthozoan.c: Anthozoan An`tho*zo"an (?), a. (Zool.) Pertaining to the Anthozoa. -- n. One of the Anthozoa.

anthozoic.c: Anthozoic An"tho*zo"ic (?), a. Of or pertaining to the Anthozoa.

anthracene.c: Anthracene An"thra*cene (?), n. [Gr. 'a`nqrax coal.] (Chem.) A solid hydrocarbon, C6H4.C2H2.C6H4, which accompanies naphthalene in the last stages of the distillation of coal tar. Its chief use is in the artificial production of alizarin. [Written also anthracin.]
Anthracene oil An"thra*cene oil (?). A heavy green oil (partially solidifying on cooling), which distills over from coal tar at a temperature above 270°. It is the principal source of anthracene.

anthracic.c: Anthracic An*thrac"ic (?), a. Of or relating to anthrax; as, anthracic blood.

anthraciferous.c: Anthraciferous An`thra*cif"er*ous (?), a. [Gr. 'a`nqrax coal + -ferous.] (Min.) Yielding anthracite; as, anthraciferous strata.

anthracite.c: Anthracite An"thra*cite (?), n. [L. anthracites a kind of bloodstone; fr. Gr.? like coals, fr. 'a`nqrax,?, coal or charcoal. Cf. Anthrax.] A hard, compact variety of mineral coal, of high luster, differing from bituminous coal in containing little or no bitumen, in consequence of which it burns with a nearly non luminous flame. The purer specimens consist almost wholly of carbon. Also called glance coal and blind coal.

anthracitic.c: Anthracitic An"thra*cit"ic (?), a. Of, pertaining to, or like, anthracite; as, anthracitic formations.

anthracnose.c: Anthracnose An*thrac"nose` (?), n. [Gr.?,?, carbuncle +? disease.] (Bot.) Any one of several fungus diseases, caused by parasitic species of the series Melanconiales, attacking the bean, grape, melon, cotton, and other plants. In the case of the grape, brown concave spots are formed on the stem and fruit, and the disease is called bird's-eye rot.

anthracoid.c: Anthracoid An"thra*coid (?), a. [Anthrax + -oid.] (Biol.) Resembling anthrax in action; of the nature of anthrax; as, an anthracoid microbe.

anthracomancy.c: Anthracomancy An"thra*co*man`cy (?), n. [Gr. 'a`nqrax, 'a`nqrakos, coal + -mancy.] Divination by inspecting a burning coal.

anthracometer.c: Anthracometer An`thra*com"e*ter (?), n. [Gr. 'a`nqrax coal, carbon + -meter.] An instrument for measuring the amount of carbonic acid in a mixture.

anthracometric.c: Anthracometric An`thra*co*met"ric (?), a. Of or pertaining to an anthracometer.

anthracosis.c: Anthracosis ‖An`thra*co"sis (?), n. [NL. See Anthrax.] (Med.) A chronic lung disease, common among coal miners, due to the inhalation of coal dust; -- called also collier's lung and miner's phthisis. See also the related conditions pneumomelanosis and pneumoconiosis (black lung).

anthraconite.c: Anthraconite An*thrac"o*nite (?), n. [See Anthracite.] (Min.) A coal-black marble, usually emitting a fetid smell when rubbed; -- called also stinkstone and swinestone.

anthraquinone.c: Anthraquinone An`thra*qui"none (?), n. [Anthracene + quinone.] (Chem.) A hydrocarbon, C6H4.C2O2.C6H4, subliming in shining yellow needles. It is obtained by oxidation of anthracene.

anthrax.c: Anthrax An"thrax (ăn"thrăks), n. [L., fr. Gr. 'a`nqrax coal, carbuncle.] 1. (Med.) (a) A carbuncle. (b) A malignant pustule.

Anthrax vaccine An"thrax vac"cine. (Veter.) A fluid vaccine obtained by growing a bacterium (Bacillus anthracis, formerly Bacterium anthracis) in beef broth. It is used to immunize animals, esp. cattle.

anthrenus.c: Anthrenus ‖An*thre"nus (ăn*thrē"nŭs), n. [NL., fr. Gr. 'anqrh`nh a hornet.] (Zool.) A genus of small beetles, several of which, in the larval state, are very destructive to woolen goods, fur, etc. The common “museum pest” is Anthrenus varius; the carpet beetle is Anthrenus scrophulariæ. The larvæ are commonly confounded with moths.

anthropical.c: Anthropical Anthropic { An*throp"ic (?), An*throp"ic*al (?), } a. [Gr.?, fr. 'a`nqrwpos man.] (Zool.) 1. Like or related to man; human. [R.] Owen.

anthropidae.c: Anthropidae ‖An*throp"i*dæ (?), n. pl. [NL., fr. Gr. 'a`nqrwpos man.] (Zool.) The group that includes man only.

anthropocentric.c: Anthropocentric An`thro*po*cen"tric (?), a. [Gr. 'a`nqrwpos man +? center.] Assuming man as the center or ultimate end; -- applied to theories of the universe or of any part of it, as the solar system. Draper.

anthropogenic.c: Anthropogenic An`thro*po*gen"ic (?), a. 1. Of or pertaining to anthropogeny.

anthropogeny.c: Anthropogeny An`thro*pog"e*ny (?), n. [Gr. 'a`nqrwpos man +? birth.] The science or study of human generation, or the origin and development of man.

anthropogeography.c: Anthropogeography An`thro*po*ge*og"ra*phy (?), n. [Gr. 'a`nqrwpos man + geography.] The science of the human species as to geographical distribution and environment. Broadly, it includes industrial, commercial, and political geography, and that part of ethnology which deals with distribution and physical environment. -- An`thro*po*ge*og"ra*pher (#), n. -- An`thro*po*ge`o*graph"ic*al (#), a.

anthropoglot.c: Anthropoglot An*throp"o*glot (?), n. [Gr.?; 'a`nqrwpos man +?,?, tongue.] (Zool.) An animal which has a tongue resembling that of man, as the parrot.

anthropography.c: Anthropography An`thro*pog"ra*phy (?), n. [Gr. 'a`nqrwpos man + -graphy.] That branch of anthropology which treats of the actual distribution of the human race in its different divisions, as distinguished by physical character, language, institutions, and customs, in contradistinction to ethnography, which treats historically of the origin and filiation of races and nations. P. Cyc.

anthropoid.c: Anthropoid An"thro*poid (?), a. [Gr. 'a`nqrwpos man + -oid.] Resembling man; -- applied especially to certain apes, as the ourang or gorilla. -- n. An anthropoid ape.

anthropoidea.c: Anthropoidea ‖An`thro*poid"e*a (?), n. pl. [NL. See Anthropoid.] (Zool.) The suborder of primates which includes the monkeys, apes, and man.

anthropolatry.c: Anthropolatry An`thro*pol"a*try (?), n. [Gr. 'a`nqrwpos man +? worship.] Man worship.

anthropolite.c: Anthropolite An*throp"o*lite (?), n. [Gr. 'a`nqrwpos man + -lite.] (Paleon.) A petrifaction of the human body, or of any portion of it.

anthropological.c: Anthropological Anthropologic { An`thro*po*log"ic (?), An`thro*po*log"ic*al (?), } a. Pertaining to anthropology; belonging to the nature of man. “Anthropologic wisdom.” Kingsley. -- An`thro*po*log"ic*al*ly, adv.

anthropologist.c: Anthropologist An`thro*pol"o*gist (?), n. One who is versed in anthropology.

anthropology.c: Anthropology An`thro*pol"o*gy (?), n. [Gr. 'a`nqrwpos man + -logy.] 1. The science of the structure and functions of the human body.

anthropomancy.c: Anthropomancy An"thro*po*man`cy (?), n. [Gr. 'a`nqrwpos man + -mancy.] Divination by the entrails of human being.

anthropometrical.c: Anthropometrical Anthropometric { An`thro*po*met"ric (?), An`thro*po*met"ric*al (?), } a. Pertaining to anthropometry.

anthropometry.c: Anthropometry An`thro*pom"e*try (?), n. [Gr. 'a`nqrwpos man + -mercy.] Measurement of the height and other dimensions of human beings, especially at different ages, or in different races, occupations, etc. Dunglison.

anthropomorpha.c: Anthropomorpha ‖An`thro*po*mor"pha (?), n. pl. [NL. See Anthropomorphism.] (Zool.) The manlike, or anthropoid, apes.

anthropomorphic.c: Anthropomorphic An`thro*po*mor"phic (?), a. Of or pertaining to anthropomorphism. Hadley. -- An`thro*po*mor"phic*al*ly (?), adv.

anthropomorphism.c: Anthropomorphism An`thro*po*mor"phism (?), n. [Gr.? of human form; 'a`nqrwpos man + morfh` form.] 1. The representation of the Deity, or of a polytheistic deity, under a human form, or with human attributes and affections.

anthropomorphist.c: Anthropomorphist An`thro*po*mor"phist (?), n. One who attributes the human form or other human attributes to the Deity or to anything not human.

anthropomorphite.c: Anthropomorphite An`thro*po*mor"phite (?), n. One who ascribes a human form or human attributes to the Deity or to a polytheistic deity. Taylor. Specifically, one of a sect of ancient heretics who believed that God has a human form, etc. Tillotson.

anthropomorphitic.c: Anthropomorphitic An`thro*po*mor*phit"ic (?), a. (Biol.) Pertaining to anthropomorphism, or anthropomorphitism. Kitto.

anthropomorphize.c: Anthropomorphize An`thro*po*mor"phize (?), v. t. & i. To attribute a human form or personality to.

anthropomorphology.c: Anthropomorphology An`thro*po*mor*phol"o*gy (?), n. [Gr.? + -logy. See Anthropomorphism.] The application to God of terms descriptive of human beings.

anthropomorphosis.c: Anthropomorphosis An`thro*po*mor"pho*sis (?), n. Transformation into the form of a human being.

anthropomorphous.c: Anthropomorphous An`thro*po*mor"phous (?), a. Having the figure of, or resemblance to, a man; as, an anthropomorphous plant. “Anthropomorphous apes.” Darwin.

anthroponomy.c: Anthroponomy Anthroponomics { An`thro*po*nom"ics (?), An`thro*pon"o*my (?) }, n.} [Gr. 'a`nqrwpos man +? usage, law, rule.] The science of the laws of the development of the human organism in relation to other organisms and to environment. -- An`thro*po*nom"ic*al (#), a.

anthropopathical.c: Anthropopathical Anthropopathic { An`thro*po*path"ic (?), An`thro*po*path"ic*al (?), } a. Of or pertaining to anthropopathy. [R.] -- An`thro*po*path"ic*al*ly, adv.

anthropopathy.c: Anthropopathy Anthropopathism { An`thro*pop"a*thism (?), An`thro*pop"a*thy (?), } n. [Gr.?; 'a`nqrwpos man +? suffering, affection, passion,?,?, to suffer.] The ascription of human feelings or passions to God, or to a polytheistic deity.

anthropopathite.c: Anthropopathite An`thro*pop"a*thite (?), n. One who ascribes human feelings to deity.

anthropophagi.c: Anthropophagi ‖An`thro*poph"a*gi (?), n. pl. [L., fr. Gr.? eating men; 'a`nqrwpos man + +? to eat.] Man eaters; cannibals. Shak.

anthropophagical.c: Anthropophagical Anthropophagic { An`thro*po*phag"ic (?), An`thro*po*phag"ic*al (?), } a. Relating to cannibalism or anthropophagy.

anthropophaginian.c: Anthropophaginian An`thro*poph`a*gin"i*an (?), n. One who east human flesh. [Ludicrous] Shak.

anthropophagite.c: Anthropophagite An`thro*poph"a*gite (?), n. A cannibal. W. Taylor.

anthropophagous.c: Anthropophagous An`thro*poph"a*gous (?), a. Feeding on human flesh; cannibal.

anthropophagy.c: Anthropophagy An`thro*poph"a*gy (?), n. [Gr.?.] The eating of human flesh; cannibalism.

anthropophuism.c: Anthropophuism An`thro*poph"u*ism (ăn`thro*pŏf"u*ĭz'm), n. [Gr. 'anqropofyh`s of man's nature; 'a`nqropos a man + fyh` nature.] Human nature. [R.] Gladstone.

anthroposcopy.c: Anthroposcopy An`thro*pos"co*py (ăn`thro*pŏs"ko*py̆), n. [Gr. 'a`nqrwpos man + -scopy.] The art of discovering or judging of a man's character, passions. and inclinations from a study of his visible features. [R.]

anthroposophy.c: Anthroposophy An`thro*pos"o*phy (ăn`thro*pŏs"o*fy̆), n. [Gr. 'a`nqrwpos man + sofi`a wisdom, knowledge.] Knowledge of the nature of man; hence, human wisdom.

anthropotomical.c: Anthropotomical An`thro*po*tom"ic*al (ăn`thro*po*tŏm"ĭ*kail), a. Pertaining to anthropotomy, or the dissection of human bodies.

anthropotomist.c: Anthropotomist An`thro*pot"o*mist (ăn`thro*pŏt"o*mĭst), n. One who is versed in anthropotomy, or human anatomy.

anthropotomy.c: Anthropotomy An`thro*pot"o*my (?), n. [Gr. 'a`nqrwpos man + tomh` a cutting.] The anatomy or dissection of the human body; androtomy. Owen.

anti.c: Anti An"ti (?). [Gr. 'anti` against. See Ante.] A prefix meaning against, opposite or opposed to, contrary, or in place of; -- used in composition in many English words. It is often shortened to ant-; as, antacid, antarctic.

antiae.c: Antiae ‖An"ti*æ (?), n. pl. [L., forelock.] (Zool.) The two projecting feathered angles of the forehead of some birds; the frontal points.

antialbumid.c: Antialbumid An`ti*al*bu"mid (?), n. [Pref. anti- + -albumin.] (Physiol. Chem.) A body formed from albumin by pancreatic and gastric digestion. It is convertible into antipeptone.

antiamerican.c: Anti-American An`ti-A*mer"i*can (?), a. Opposed to the Americans, their aims, or interests, or to the genius of American institutions. Marshall.

antiaphrodisiac.c: Antiaphrodisiac An`ti*aph`ro*dis"i*ac (?), a. & n. Same as Antaphrodisiac.

antiapoplectic.c: Antiapoplectic An`ti*ap`o*plec"tic (?), a. & n. (Med.) Same as Antapoplectic.

antiar.c: Antiar An"ti*ar (?), n. [Jav. antjar.] A Virulent poison prepared in Java from the gum resin of one species of the upas tree (Antiaris toxicaria).

antiarin.c: Antiarin An`ti*a*rin (?), n. (Chem.) A poisonous principle obtained from antiar. Watts.

antiasthmatic.c: Antiasthmatic An`ti*asth*mat"ic (?), a. & n. Same as Antasthmatic.

antiattrition.c: Antiattrition An`ti*at*tri"tion (?), n. Anything to prevent the effects of friction, esp. a compound lubricant for machinery, etc., often consisting of plumbago, with some greasy material; antifriction grease.

antibacchius.c: Antibacchius ‖An`ti*bac*chi"us (?), n. [L., fr. Gr. 'anti` +?. See Bacchius.] (Pros.) A foot of three syllables, the first two long, and the last short (#).

antibacterial.c: Antibacterial An`ti*bac*te"ri*al (?), a. (Med.) (a) killing or inhibiting the growth of bacteria; -- applied also to serum for protection against bacterial diseases. (b) Opposed to the bacterial theory of disease. [archaic]

antibillous.c: Antibillous An`ti*bil"lous (?), a. Counteractive of bilious complaints; tending to relieve biliousness.

antibody.c: Antibody An"ti*bod`y (ăn"tĭ*bŏd`y̆), n. 1. (Med., Physiol. Chem.) Any of various bodies or substances in the blood which act in antagonism to harmful foreign bodies, as toxins or the bacteria producing the toxins. Normal blood serum apparently contains various antibodies, and the introduction of toxins or of foreign cells also stimulates production of their specific antibodies by the immune system.

antibrachial.c: Antibrachial An`ti*brach"i*al (?), a. (Anat.) Of or pertaining to the antibrachium, or forearm.

antibrachium.c: Antibrachium ‖An`ti*brach"i*um (?), n. [NL.] (Anat.) That part of the fore limb between the brachium and the carpus; the forearm.

antibromic.c: Antibromic An`ti*bro"mic (?), n. [Pref. anti- + Gr.? a stink.] An agent that destroys offensive smells; a deodorizer.

antibubonic.c: Antibubonic An`ti*bu*bon"ic (?), a. Good or used against bubonic plague; as, antibubonic serum, obtained from immunized horses; antibubonic vaccine, a sterilized bouillon culture of the plague bacillus; antibubonic measures.

antiburgher.c: Antiburgher An`ti*burgh"er (-bûrg"ẽr), n. (Eccl. Hist.) One who seceded from the Scottish Burghers (1747), deeming it improper to take the Burgess oath.

antic.c: Antic An"tic (ăn"tĭk), a. [The same word as antique; cf. It. antico ancient. See Antique.] 1. Old; antique. (Zool.) “Lords of antic fame.” Phaer.
Antic An"tic, n. 1. A buffoon or merry-andrew; one that practices odd gesticulations; the Fool of the old play.
Antic An"tic, v. t. [imp. & p. p. Anticked (?), Antickt.] To make appear like a buffoon. [Obs.] Shak.
Antic An"tic, v. i. To perform antics.

anticatarrhal.c: Anticatarrhal An`ti*ca*tarrh`al (?), a. (Med.) Efficacious against catarrh. -- n. An anticatarrhal remedy.

anticathode.c: Anticathode An`ti*cath"ode (?), n. (Phys.) The part of a vacuum tube opposite the cathode. Upon it the cathode rays impinge.

anticausodic.c: Anticausodic An`ti*cau*sod"ic (?), a. & n. (Med.) Same as Anticausotic.

anticausotic.c: Anticausotic An`ti*cau*sot"ic (?), a. [Pref. anti- + Gr.? fever,? to burn.] (Med.) Good against an inflammatory fever. -- n. A remedy for such a fever.

antichlor.c: Antichlor An"ti*chlor (?), n. [Pref. anti- + chlorine.] (Chem.) Any substance (but especially sodium hyposulphite) used in removing the excess of chlorine left in paper pulp or stuffs after bleaching.

antichrist.c: Antichrist An"ti*christ (?), n. [L. Antichristus, Gr.?; 'anti` against +?.] A denier or opponent of Christ. Specif.: A great antagonist, person or power, expected to precede Christ's second coming.

antichristian.c: Antichristian An`ti*chris"tian (?; 106), a. Opposed to the Christian religion.

antichristianity.c: Antichristianity Antichristianism { An`ti*chris"tian*ism (?), An`ti*chris*tian"i*ty (?), } n. Opposition or contrariety to the Christian religion.

antichristianly.c: Antichristianly An`ti*chris"tian*ly (?), adv. In an antichristian manner.

antichronical.c: Antichronical An`ti*chron"ic*al (?), a. Deviating from the proper order of time. -- An`ti*chron"ic*al*ly, adv.

antichronism.c: Antichronism An*tich"ro*nism (?), n. [Gr.?; 'anti` against +? time.] Deviation from the true order of time; anachronism. [R.] Selden.

antichthon.c: Antichthon ‖An*tich"thon (?), n.; pl. Antichthones (?). [Gr.?; 'anti` against +? the earth.] 1. A hypothetical earth counter to ours, or on the opposite side of the sun. Grote.

anticipant.c: Anticipant An*tic"i*pant (?), a. [L. anticipans, p. pr. of anticipare.] Anticipating; expectant; -- with of.

anticipate.c: Anticipate An*tic"i*pate (?), v. t. [imp. & p. p. Anticipated (?); p. pr. & vb. n. Anticipating (?).] [L. anticipatus, p. p. of anticipare to anticipate; ante + capere to make. See Capable.] 1. To be before in doing; to do or take before another; to preclude or prevent by prior action.

anticipation.c: Anticipation An*tic`i*pa"tion (ăn`tĭs`ĭ*pā"shŭn), n. [L. anticipatio: cf. F. anticipation.] 1. The act of anticipating, taking up, placing, or considering something beforehand, or before the proper time in natural order.

anticipative.c: Anticipative An*tic"i*pa*tive (ăn`tĭs"ĭ*pa*tĭv), a. Anticipating, or containing anticipation. “Anticipative of the feast to come.” Cary. -- An*tic"i*pa*tive*ly, adv.

anticipatory.c: Anticipatory An*tic"i*pa*to*ry (ăn`tĭs"ĭ*pȧ*to*ry̆), a. Forecasting; of the nature of anticipation. Owen.

anticivism.c: Anticivism An`ti*civ"ism (ăn`tĭ*cĭv"ĭz'm), n. Opposition to the body politic of citizens. [Obs.] Carlyle.

anticlastic.c: Anticlastic An`ti*clas"tic (ăn`tĭ*klăs"tĭk), a. [Pref. anti- = Gr. kla^n to break.] Having opposite curvatures, that is, curved longitudinally in one direction and transversely in the opposite direction, as the surface of a saddle.

anticlimax.c: Anticlimax An`ti*cli"max (?), n. (Rhet.) A sentence in which the ideas fall, or become less important and striking, at the close; -- the opposite of climax. It produces a ridiculous effect. Example:

anticlinal.c: Anticlinal An`ti*cli"nal (ăn`tĭ*klī"nail), a. [Pref. anti- + Gr. kli`nein to incline.] 1. Inclining or dipping in opposite directions. See Synclinal.
Anticlinal An`ti*cli"nal, n. (Geol.) The crest or line in which strata slope or dip in opposite directions.

anticline.c: Anticline An"ti*cline (?), n. [See Anticlinal.] (Geol.) A structure of bedded rocks in which the beds on both sides of an axis or axial plane dip away from the axis; an anticlinal. Contrassted with syncline.

anticlinorium.c: Anticlinorium ‖An`ti*cli*no"ri*um (?), n.; pl. Anticlinoria (?). [NL., fr. Gr. 'anti` against + kli`nein to incline + 'o`ros mountain.] (Geol.) The upward elevation of the crust of the earth, resulting from a geanticlinal.

anticmask.c: Antic-mask An"tic-mask` (?), n. An antimask. B. Jonson.

anticness.c: Anticness An"tic*ness, n. The quality of being antic. Ford.

anticoherer.c: Anticoherer An`ti*co*her"er (?), n. (Wireless Teleg.) A device, one form of which consists of a scratched deposit of silver on glass, used in connection with the receiving apparatus for reading wireless signals. The electric waves falling on this contrivance increase its resistance several times. The anticoherer can be used in conjunction with a telephone.

anticonstitutional.c: Anticonstitutional An`ti*con`sti*tu"tion*al (?), a. Opposed to the constitution; unconstitutional.

anticontagious.c: Anticontagious An`ti*con*ta"gious (?), a. (Med.) Opposing or destroying contagion.

anticonvulsive.c: Anticonvulsive An`ti*con*vul"sive (?), a. (Med.) Good against convulsions. J. Floyer.

anticor.c: Anticor An"ti*cor (?), n. [Pref. anti- + L. cor heart; cf. F. antic?ur.] (Far.) A dangerous inflammatory swelling of a horse's breast, just opposite the heart.

anticous.c: Anticous An*ti"cous (?), a. [L. anticus in front, foremost, fr. ante before.] (Bot.) Facing toward the axis of the flower, as in the introrse anthers of the water lily.

anticyclone.c: Anticyclone An"ti*cy`clone (ăn"tĭ*sī`klōn), n. (Meteorol.) A movement of the atmosphere opposite in character, as regards direction of the wind and distribution of barometric pressure, to that of a cyclone. -- An`ti*cy*clon"ic (?), a. -- An`ti*cy*clon"ic*al*ly (?), adv.

antidiphtheritic.c: Antidiphtheritic An`ti*diph`the*rit"ic (?), a. (Med.) Destructive to, or hindering the growth of, diphtheria bacilli. -- n. An antidiphtheritic agent.

antidotal.c: Antidotal An"ti*do`tal (ăn"tĭ*dō`tail)(#) a. Having the quality an antidote; fitted to counteract the effects of poison. Sir T. Browne. -- An"ti*do`tal*ly, adv.

antidotary.c: Antidotary An"ti*do`ta*ry (ăn"tĭ*dō`tȧ*ry̆), a. Antidotal. -- n. An antidote; also, a book of antidotes.

antidote.c: Antidote An"ti*dote (ăn"tĭ*dōt), n. [L. antidotum, Gr. 'anti`doton (sc. fa`rmakon), fr. 'anti`dotos given against; 'anti` against + dido`nai to give: cf. F. antidote. See Dose, n.] 1. A remedy to counteract the effects of poison, or of anything noxious taken into the stomach; -- used with against, for, or to; as, an antidote against, for, or to, poison.
Antidote An"ti*dote, v. t. 1. To counteract or prevent the effects of, by giving or taking an antidote.

antidotical.c: Antidotical An`ti*dot"ic*al (ăn`tĭ*dōt"ĭ*kail), a. Serving as an antidote. -- An`ti*dot"ic*al*ly, adv.

antidromous.c: Antidromous An*tid"ro*mous (ăn*tĭd"ro*mŭs), a. [Pref. anti- + Gr. dro`mos a running.] (Bot.) Changing the direction in the spiral sequence of leaves on a stem.

antidysenteric.c: Antidysenteric An`ti*dys`en*ter"ic (?), a. (Med.) Good against dysentery. -- n. A medicine for dysentery.

antiemetic.c: Antiemetic An`ti*e*met"ic (?), a. & n. (Med.) Same as Antemetic.

antiephialtic.c: Antiephialtic An`ti*eph`i*al"tic (?), a. & n. (Med.) Same as Antephialtic.

antiepileptic.c: Antiepileptic An`ti*ep`i*lep"tic (?), a. & n. (Med.) Same as Antepileptic.

antifederalist.c: Anti-federalist An`ti-fed"er*al*ist (?), n. One of party opposed to a federative government; -- applied particularly to the party which opposed the adoption of the constitution of the United States. Pickering.

antifriction.c: Antifriction An`ti*fric"tion (?), n. Something to lessen friction; antiattrition. -- a. Tending to lessen friction.

antigalastic.c: Antigalastic An`ti*ga*las"tic (?), a. [Pref. anti- + Gr.?,?, milk.] Causing a diminution or a suppression of the secretion of milk.

antigallican.c: Anti-Gallican An`ti-Gal"li*can (?), a. Opposed to what is Gallic or French.

antigraph.c: Antigraph An"ti*graph (?), n. [Gr.? a transcribing: cf. F. antigraphe.] A copy or transcript.

antiguggler.c: Antiguggler An`ti*gug"gler (?) n. [Pref. anti- + guggle or gurgle.] A crooked tube of metal, to be introduced into the neck of a bottle for drawing out the liquid without disturbing the sediment or causing a gurgling noise.

antihelix.c: Antihelix An`ti*he"lix (?), n. (Anat.) The curved elevation of the cartilage of the ear, within or in front of the helix. See Ear.

antihemorrhagic.c: Antihemorrhagic An`ti*hem`or*rhag"ic (?), a. (Med.) Tending to stop hemorrhage. -- n. A remedy for hemorrhage.

antihydrophobic.c: Antihydrophobic An`ti*hy`dro*phob"ic (?), a. (Med.) Counteracting or preventing hydrophobia. -- n. A remedy for hydrophobia.

antihydropic.c: Antihydropic An`ti*hy*drop"ic (?), a. (Med.) Good against dropsy. -- n. A remedy for dropsy.

antihypnotic.c: Antihypnotic An`ti*hyp*not"ic (?), a. (Med.) Tending to prevent sleep. -- n. An antihypnotic agent.

antihypochondriac.c: Antihypochondriac An`ti*hyp`o*chon"dri*ac (?), a. (Med.) Counteractive of hypochondria. -- n. A remedy for hypochondria.

antihysteric.c: Antihysteric An`ti*hys*ter"ic (?), a. (Med.) Counteracting hysteria. -- n. A remedy for hysteria.

antiicteric.c: Antiicteric An`ti*ic*ter"ic (?), a. (Med.) Good against jaundice. -- n. A remedy for jaundice.

antiimperialism.c: Anti-imperialism An`ti-im*pe"ri*al*ism (?), n. Opposition to imperialism. -- An`ti-im*pe"ri*al*ist, n. -- An`ti-im*pe`ri*al*is"tic (#), a.

antilegomena.c: Antilegomena ‖An`ti*le*gom"e*na (?), n. pl. [NL., fr. Gr. 'anti` against +? to speak; part. pass.?.] (Eccl.) Certain books of the New Testament which were for a time not universally received, but which are now considered canonical. These are the Epistle to the Hebrews, the Epistles of James and Jude, the second Epistle of Peter, the second and third Epistles of John, and the Revelation. The undisputed books are called the Homologoumena.

antilibration.c: Antilibration An`ti*li*bra"tion (?), n. A balancing; equipoise. [R.] De Quincey.

antilithic.c: Antilithic An`ti*lith"ic (?), a. (Med.) Tending to prevent the formation of urinary calculi, or to destroy them when formed. -- n. An antilithic medicine.

antilogarithm.c: Antilogarithm An`ti*log"a*rithm (?), n. (Math.) The number corresponding to a logarithm. The word has been sometimes, though rarely, used to denote the complement of a given logarithm; also the logarithmic cosine corresponding to a given logarithmic sine. -- An`ti*log`a*rith"mic (?), a.

antilogous.c: Antilogous An*til"o*gous (ăn*tĭl"o*gŭs), a. Of the contrary name or character; -- opposed to analogous.

antilogy.c: Antilogy An*til"o*gy (ăn*tĭl"o*jy̆), n.; pl. Antilogies (-jĭz). [Gr. 'antilogi`a, fr. 'anti`logos contradictory; 'anti` against + le`gein to speak.] A contradiction between any words or passages in an author. Sir W. Hamilton.

antiloimic.c: Antiloimic An`ti*loi"mic (ăn`tĭ*loi"mĭk), n. (Med.) A remedy against the plague. Brande & C.

antilopine.c: Antilopine An*til"o*pine (ăn*tĭl"o*pīn), a. Of or relating to the antelope.

antiloquy.c: Antiloquy An*til"o*quy (acr/n*tĭl"o*kwy̆), n. [Pref. anti- + L. loqui to speak.] Contradiction. [Obs.]

antilyssic.c: Antilyssic An`ti*lys"sic (ăn`tĭ*lĭs"sĭk), a. & n. [Pref. anti- + Gr.? rage, madness.] (Med.) Antihydrophobic.

antimacassar.c: Antimacassar An`ti*ma*cas"sar (ăn`tĭ*mȧ*kăs"sẽr), n. A cover for the back or arms of a chair or sofa, etc., to prevent them from wear or from being soiled by macassar or other oil from the hair.

antimagistrical.c: Antimagistrical An`ti*ma*gis"tric*al (ăn`tĭ*mȧ*jĭs"trĭ*kail), a. [Pref. anti- + magistrical for magistratical.] Opposed to the office or authority of magistrates. [Obs.] South.

antimask.c: Antimask An"ti*mask` (ăn"tĭ*mȧsk`), n. A secondary mask, or grotesque interlude, between the parts of a serious mask. [Written also antimasque.] Bacon.

antimason.c: Antimason An`ti*ma"son (ăn`tĭ*mā"s'n), n. One opposed to Freemasonry. -- An`ti*ma*son"ic (ăn`tĭ*mȧ*sŏn"ĭk), a.

antimephitic.c: Antimephitic An`ti*me*phit"ic (?), a. (Med.) Good against mephitic or deleterious gases. -- n. A remedy against mephitic gases. Dunglison.

antimere.c: Antimere An"ti*mere (?), n. [. anti- + -mere.] (Biol.) One of the two halves of bilaterally symmetrical animals; one of any opposite symmetrical or homotypic parts in animals and plants.

antimetabole.c: Antimetabole ‖An`ti*me*tab"o*le (?), n. [L., fr. Gr.?.] (Rhet.) A figure in which the same words or ideas are repeated in transposed order.

antimetathesis.c: Antimetathesis ‖An`ti*me*tath"e*sis (?), n. [NL., fr. Gr.?.] (Rhet.) An antithesis in which the members are repeated in inverse order.

antimeter.c: Antimeter An*tim"e*ter (?), n. [Gr.? like +? measure.] A modification of the quadrant, for measuring small angles. [Obs.]

antimonarchical.c: Antimonarchical Antimonarchic { An`ti*mo*nar"chic (?), An`ti*mo*nar"chic*al (?), } Opposed to monarchial government. Bp. Benson. Addison.

antimonarchist.c: Antimonarchist An`ti*mon"arch*ist (?), n. An enemy to monarchial government.

antimonate.c: Antimonate An`ti*mo"nate (?), n. (Chem.) A compound of antimonic acid with a base or basic radical. [Written also antimoniate.]

antimonial.c: Antimonial An`ti*mo"ni*al (?), a. Of or pertaining to antimony. -- n. (Med.) A preparation or medicine containing antimony.

antimoniated.c: Antimoniated An`ti*mo"ni*a`ted (?), a. Combined or prepared with antimony; as, antimoniated tartar.

antimonic.c: Antimonic An`ti*mon"ic (?), a. (Chem.) Pertaining to, or derived from, antimony; -- said of those compounds of antimony in which this element has its highest equivalence; as, antimonic acid.

antimonious.c: Antimonious An`ti*mo"ni*ous (?), a. (Chem.) Pertaining to, or derived from, antimony; -- said of those compounds of antimony in which this element has an equivalence next lower than the highest; as, antimonious acid.

antimonite.c: Antimonite An"ti*mo*nite` (?), n. 1. (Chem.) A compound of antimonious acid and a base or basic radical.

antimoniureted.c: Antimoniureted An`ti*mo"ni*u*ret`ed (?), a. (Chem.) Combined with or containing antimony; as, antimoniureted hydrogen. [Written also antimoniuretted.]

antimonsoon.c: Antimonsoon An"ti*mon*soon" (?), n. (Meteor.) The upper, contrary-moving current of the atmosphere over a monsoon.

antimony.c: Antimony An"ti*mo*ny (ăn"tĭ*mo*ny̆; 112), n. [LL. antimonium, of unknown origin.] (Chem.) An elementary substance, resembling a metal in its appearance and physical properties, but in its chemical relations belonging to the class of nonmetallic substances. Atomic weight, 120. Symbol, Sb.

antinational.c: Antinational An`ti*na"tion*al (ăn"tĭ*năsh"ŭn*ail), a. Antagonistic to one's country or nation, or to a national government.

antinephritic.c: Antinephritic An`ti*ne*phrit"ic (ăn"tĭ*ne*frĭt"ĭk), a. (Med.) Counteracting, or deemed of use in, diseases of the kidneys. -- n. An antinephritic remedy.

antinomian.c: Antinomian An`ti*no"mi*an (?), a. [See Antimony.] Of or pertaining to the Antinomians; opposed to the doctrine that the moral law is obligatory.

Antinomian An`ti*no"mi*an, n. (Eccl. Hist.) One who maintains that, under the gospel dispensation, the moral law is of no use or obligation, but that faith alone is necessary to salvation. The sect of Antinomians originated with John Agricola, in Germany, about the year 1535. Mosheim.

antinomianism.c: Antinomianism An`ti*no"mi*an*ism (?), n. The tenets or practice of Antinomians. South.

antinomist.c: Antinomist An*tin"o*mist (?), n. An Antinomian. [R.] Bp. Sanderson.

antinomy.c: Antinomy An*tin"o*my (?; 277), n.; pl. Antinomies (?). [L. antinomia, Gr.?; 'anti` against +? law.] 1. Opposition of one law or rule to another law or rule.

antiochian.c: Antiochian An`ti*o"chi*an (?), a. 1. Pertaining to Antiochus, a contemporary with Cicero, and the founder of a sect of philosophers.

antiodontalgic.c: Antiodontalgic An`ti*o`don*tal"gic (?), a. (Med.) Efficacious in curing toothache. -- n. A remedy for toothache.

antiorgastic.c: Antiorgastic An`ti*or*gas"tic (?), a. [Pref. anti- + Gr.? to swell, as with lust.] (Med.) Tending to allay venereal excitement or desire; sedative.

antipapal.c: Antipapal An`ti*pa"pal (?), a. Opposed to the pope or to popery. Milton.

antiparallel.c: Antiparallel An`ti*par"al*lel (?), a. Running in a contrary direction. Hammond.

antiparallels.c: Antiparallels An`ti*par"al*lels (?), n. pl. (Geom.) Straight lines or planes which make angles in some respect opposite in character to those made by parallel lines or planes.

antiparalytic.c: Antiparalytic An`ti*par`a*lyt"ic (?), a. (Med.) Good against paralysis. -- n. A medicine for paralysis.

antipasch.c: Antipasch An"ti*pasch (?), n. [Pref. anti- + pasch.] (Eccl.) The Sunday after Easter; Low Sunday.

antipathetical.c: Antipathetical Antipathetic { An`ti*pa*thet"ic (?), An`ti*pa*thet"ic*al (?), } a. Having a natural contrariety, or constitutional aversion, to a thing; characterized by antipathy; -- often followed by to. Fuller.

antipathic.c: Antipathic An`ti*path"ic (?), a. [NL. antipathicus, Gr.? of opposite feelings.] (Med.) Belonging to antipathy; opposite; contrary; allopathic.

antipathist.c: Antipathist An*tip"a*thist (ăn*tĭp"ȧ*thĭst), n. One who has an antipathy. [R.] “Antipathist of light.” Coleridge.
